sections.title: Other project ideas
paragraphs: The following pros and cons are retrospective assessments added to this report. They are not confirmed statements from the meeting or reasons for individual votes.

tables.label: Project idea comparison
rows: Docent: multilingual exhibition guide
A clear setting for follow-up questions and multilingual conversation.
Official exhibition materials can ground answers.
A pilot can start with one exhibit and one tablet.
Realistic testing needs an exhibition partner.
Noise and reluctance to speak in public may limit use.
Content updates and answer checks require ongoing work.
VoiceQuest: multiplayer voice mystery game
Team members can test the game together.
The game tests turn-taking, interruptions, and shared context.
One short mystery gives the prototype a clear scope.
Enjoyment depends heavily on story quality.
Simultaneous speakers make interaction difficult.
Spoilers or inconsistent clues can break the game.
VoiceFit: voice-controlled workout assistant
Hands-free control addresses a concrete inconvenience.
Timers, pauses, and corrections give measurable tasks.
User-defined routines reduce the need for specialist content.
Existing timers may already meet user needs.
Breathing and background noise can reduce recognition quality.
Incorrect timing or commands can disrupt exercise.
Reservation assistant: AI phone bookings
The service completes a concrete task.
It can reach businesses without online booking.
It tests conversation, negotiation, and delegated actions.
Phone integration adds cost and complexity.
Staff may decline or struggle with AI calls.
Ambiguous answers can cause incorrect booking confirmations.
Voice body double: help with task completion
The service addresses difficulty starting and finishing tasks.
It tests proactive check-ins and persistent task state.
Completion and repeat use give concrete evaluation measures.
Check-ins may feel intrusive or like nagging.
Scheduling and reconnection add complexity.
Use may decline after the initial novelty fades.
FamilySync: shared family scheduling
The service addresses recurring coordination needs.
It tests multi-user context and consent.
A three-person scenario gives a focused prototype.
Adoption needs participation from several family members.
Speaker identification and calendar access add complexity.
Permission or schedule errors can undermine trust.

after.title: Service role: everyday reflection
paragraphs: The team explored help with expressing and organizing everyday thoughts, with a lighter role than specialized mental healthcare.

after.title: Speak, organize, gain distance, notice patterns
items: A hands-free brain dump could let users speak freely instead of typing, then review an organized account of their day.
Distance from their thoughts may help users view situations more objectively and notice recurring triggers or patterns. A personal checklist was suggested.

after.title: Conditions for use and trust
items: Users need private time and a space where they can speak comfortably. Some users value writing by hand, so the team must examine when speech is useful.
People may share worries with a trusted listener who helps them notice assumptions, biases, mistaken judgments, or leaps in reasoning. A diary or spoken account can still be selective or incomplete.

records.title: Third regular meetup: voice tarot and team development
records.venue: Hyundai Motor and Kia headquarters, Yangjae
records.summary: The team changed the MIND DETOXING concept to voice tarot. The first version will use a mobile website with an immediate voice connection. The product name and voice provider remain open.

sections.title: Decisions from the meeting
items: Build a two-way tarot conversation. The user explains a question, selects a card, hears an interpretation, and asks follow-up questions.
Start with a mobile website. The user starts a voice session inside the website. A telephone number is not necessary.
Use a cute, playful visual direction. The team still needs to choose the character and detailed design.
Consider scheduled calls and payments after the immediate connection works.
Let members work on features across disciplines. Product, frontend, and backend coordinators will help resolve differences.
The goal is a working product and a successful December 16 demo. Sona remains an optional tool.

sections.title: What the discussion clarified
items: The same product description led to different expectations. The specification must show the screens and conversation sequence together.
The reader must speak the interpretation. A spoken greeting followed by a text-only result does not meet the intended experience.
Do tests of Korean pronunciation, response delay, interruption, and character tone with real conversations.
Compare OpenAI and ElevenLabs before the provider decision. Their APIs have different interfaces.

sections.title: Progress and remaining work
items: The team selected the product direction. A working product and live voice test results are not yet available.
The next checkpoint is one complete mobile flow: start, conversation, card selection, spoken interpretation, and end.
The proposed schedule has a November 30 demo milestone. Presentation practice follows. The submission dates need confirmation from the organizer.
The leader will prepare the first specification, API comparison, and shared development setup. Members will review the specification and select tasks.
Make a decision about the intended users, name, character, provider, cost limits, hosting, and task owners.

sections.title: GitHub and Codex workflow proposal
items: These are proposed rules for development after v1.0. The meeting did not approve these detailed procedures.
Create an Issue before each task. Record the purpose, scope, acceptance criteria, owner, and reviewer.
Create one branch per task from the latest main branch. Do not commit directly to main.
Ask Codex to read AGENTS.md and the Issue. Examine its plan before implementation.
Open a small draft pull request early. Include the Issue, reason for the change, test results, and screenshots when applicable.
Ask another member to examine the change and user flow. Use Codex code review as additional help.
The leader is the first integration maintainer. This person examines the peer review and CI results before a squash merge.
Another member must examine the leader’s changes. Select a second integration maintainer for absences.
Resolve conflicts with the other task owner. Ask the relevant coordinator for help with product or interface decisions.
Use CI for type checks, lint checks, tests, and the build. Use test adapters without production secrets or paid API calls.
Deploy main to a test environment after checks pass. Check the main user flow before deployment to the demo environment.
Use GitHub Projects: Backlog, Ready, In progress, In review, and Done. Mark work Done after deployment verification.
Keep keys, raw audio, and personal conversations out of the repository. Record contributions through results, reviews, tests, and documentation.
Ask each member about preferred work, available time, blockers, and support needs. Record important decisions in the repository.

sections.title: User journey
items: Social login screen: Naver, Kakao, and OpenAI.
Nickname screen: user input with a random default value.
Main screen: reader profile card and a call button that opens the call screen.
Call screen: mute and end controls at the bottom, with a real-time activity effect at the top.
The user speaks three card numbers from 78 predefined cards. The interface shows a card draw effect.
The voice agent explains each selected card, then continues the consultation through voice interaction.
The call ends when credits are exhausted or the user selects the end button. The report screen then opens.
The report shows the selected cards at the top and the conversation summary below. Show a loading state during summary generation, then return to the main screen.

sections.title: Character and service concept

sections.title: Cost and payment direction
items: Use passes in 10-minute units. A 7-minute consultation uses one pass; a 27-minute consultation uses three passes. Unused time is discarded.
Decide later whether to offer a free trial without membership, with API cost as a constraint.

sections.title: Challenges and adjustments

records.title: Fifth regular meetup: voice, design, and MVP architecture
records.venue: Hyundai Motor and Kia headquarters, Yangjae
records.summary: The team reviewed voice candidates, selected a visual direction, and discussed infrastructure and product policies. Follow-up work and unresolved decisions are recorded as of the meeting.

sections.title: Voice models
items: The team discussed latency in the current OpenAI text to ElevenLabs speech pipeline and a possible provider change. Streaming, WebSocket support, and latency require verification.
The team tested Typecast voices including Miran and Gain. Some preferred their Korean naturalness. Speed, emotion, and tone controls and different tones for readings and questions were discussed.

sections.title: Visual direction
items: The team favored the 1108 metallic concept with Y2K analog elements, a blurred star background, and silver and gray tones.
A Western blonde Barbie-style mascot was selected as a reference. Original or appropriately licensed assets and rights review are needed for the mascot and planned 78-card illustrations.
Each designer will prepare three font candidates. Intro sound effects or subtle background music remain under consideration.

sections.title: Infrastructure and development
items: Use Vercel initially for MVP speed and defer AWS due to management overhead. The team plans to share costs.
Use a monorepo for web, future mobile, backend, specifications, and documentation. A Git Flow guide covering branches and commits was completed.
React and TypeScript frontend setup is in progress. Define user and report properties, database schema, and REST APIs.

sections.title: Product questions
items: Reaffirmed 10-minute charging units and expiration of unused time within a session. Revisit the 10-, 20-, and 30-minute labels and assess a new-user trial after checking API cost.
The discussed initial target was women in their late teens through their 30s. Check legal requirements for minors.
Decide between button and voice-command ending, recognizing voice recognition may fail. Categorize concerns such as relationships and work.
Social compatibility readings are a post-MVP idea. Storing voice conversations for feedback with optional consent was discussed; the policy remains open.

sections.title: Follow-up work and original deadlines

Prepare three font candidates per designer. Upload UI v1.0 to Figma by November 12 at midnight and complete the team vote by November 13 at 12:00.

Prepare a design and voice integration before November 15 and collect references for 78 card illustrations. Draft the database schema, user and report properties, and REST API list. Completion of these planned tasks has not been verified.

sections.title: Product direction
items: Ten Minute is the leading name. Whether to include tarot or use Korean remains open. Focus on relationship questions while keeping free consultation; suggested topics are optional, and the model classifies concerns from the conversation.

sections.title: Report and spreads
items: Provide four spreads to the model and ask it to select one: past, present, future; situation, obstacle, advice; me, the other person, relationship; or option A, option B, advice.
Reveal the cards one at a time. The personal report includes card images, consultation date and time, a short message from the reader, and a one-line situation summary.

sections.title: Sharing
items: Share a URL with a light, compelling thumbnail and a Try it myself button on the destination. The full personal report stays private; share images focus on a hook. Masking is excluded due to complexity, and preselected topics are preferred for viral sharing.

sections.title: Persona and voice
items: Use a cool, direct style inspired by Lee Hyori. Give short feedback suited to the situation rather than long card explanations. Test prompt instructions for a faster conversational tempo.

The team observed a timing mismatch between drawing a card and interpreting it. Consider a separate backend agent or model for card tasks. The meeting compared Live API and Realtime API speed controls; verify capabilities during implementation.

Deploy frontend and backend projects on Vercel. Separate the database and authentication server from the Realtime API relay. Buy and connect a domain.

Each member will improve and test prompts based on SOUL.md, write few-shot examples by relationship scenario, and try comparable phone consultation services and share feedback. Record the experience if possible.

report.title: Executive summary
report.guidance: State the user problem and the project scope. Give the primary results and limitations.
paragraphs: Voice UX Lab is an eight-week study of voice-first AI interaction and collaborative development. The team built Ten Minutes, a mobile voice tarot prototype with interactive card selection and personal reports.

As of November 27, basic login and consultation were reported to work in device tests. The team was preparing the submission build; full acceptance, measured voice quality and presentation outcomes are not yet verified.

report.title: Problem & research questions
report.guidance: Give the task, user needs, research questions, and success criteria.
paragraphs: Voice offers a natural medium for a personal conversation, but precise selections and persistent results benefit from a screen. Ten Minutes explores the balance between those two interaction modes.
The team investigated Korean speech naturalness, character consistency, turn-taking, session pacing and the alignment of conversation with application state.

report.title: Agent & demo
report.guidance: Add links to the demo, source code, video, and setup instructions. List the tasks that the agent can do.
paragraphs: The prototype combines voice conversation, question clarification, a selection from 78 cards, sequential interpretation and a personal report. The current demonstration is a working prototype, not a claim of a completed commercial product.
The public repository contains setup instructions. Demo availability can vary while integration testing continues. A recording and final presentation will be added when approved and available.

report.title: Design & architecture
report.guidance: Show the system design and the voice interface. Include tool calls, handoffs, and guardrails only if the project uses them. Give the reasons for design decisions.
paragraphs: The application uses a React and TypeScript mobile web frontend, a FastAPI backend, PostgreSQL and Vercel. The browser connects to OpenAI Realtime over WebRTC; model response text is synthesized into speech through Typecast.
Application-controlled actions coordinate card selection and reveal with the conversational agent. The backend manages consultation state, card data and report persistence.
The hybrid approach supports voice selection but requires explicit handling of interruption, playback timing, and reconnection.

report.title: Development & technical insights
report.guidance: State which development tasks used the API and Codex. Give each technical problem, its solution, and the checks of that solution.
paragraphs: The team moved from scripted proofs of concept to a structured React and TypeScript application, then integrated voice, card selection and report handling. The design evolved through visual concept review and a complete deck of 78 card illustrations.

Codex supported software development. The team established feature specifications, a monorepo and a Git Flow with feature branches, pull requests, development integration and release checks. Human review was important in refining the voice persona and dialogue.

tables.label: Technical learning
rows: Hybrid voice response
Naturalness and timing must be tested together.
Voice and visual synchronization
Use a consistent application state for card reveal and interpretation.
Cross-device testing
Test the real journey on mobile browsers instead of relying only on local checks.
Session lifecycle
Handle endings, disconnects and reports as part of the complete experience.
Design integration
Compare the deployed interface with the design and product specification.

report.title: Evaluation & improvement
report.guidance: Give the test method, scenarios, measures, results, failures, and improvements. Keep observations separate from conclusions.
paragraphs: Members conducted exploratory service research and prototype tests. Qualitative observations concerned ease of entry, participation in card selection, response pacing, naturalness and closing.
Basic device checks were reported by November 27. These observations do not establish user satisfaction, reliability, or quantitative latency. Further controlled tests are required.

report.title: Study records
report.guidance: Give each week’s work and the changes to the problem, design, and implementation.
paragraphs: The journey began with orientation and a group vote for MIND DETOXING. The team then chose voice tarot and explored several interaction and visual concepts.
Later weeks focused on the initial prototype, voice-provider evaluation, visual design, engineering foundation, user research, prompt refinement and integration testing. Week 8 remains in progress.

report.title: Individual work & reflections
report.guidance: Add each member’s approved name, role, work links, and comments. Keep meeting attendance separate from program completion.
paragraphs: The team collaborated across product planning, UX design, frontend, backend, voice and prompt development. Tasks, handoffs and review were coordinated through shared specifications, pull requests and design review.
The study encouraged members to explore work outside their original areas of expertise. Individual names and reflections will be included only with approval.

report.title: Limitations & next steps
report.guidance: List the problems that remain and the limits of the tests. State which functions need more work.
paragraphs: The team has not completed formal evaluation of voice naturalness, latency, interruption handling, full device compatibility or end-to-end reliability. Exploratory research cannot be generalized to the broader market.

Payments, repeated card draws, expanded reader options and broader research remain follow-up work. The November 27 deadline is for submission, not proof of a finished release. The planned presentation is December 16.

report.title: Artifacts & references
report.guidance: Add the code, documents, presentation, demo video, approved photos, evidence index, and source links.
paragraphs: Public evidence includes the product repository, feature specifications, Git Flow and card asset documentation. Private research transcripts, personal information, credentials, restricted designs and operational records are not part of this archive.
Additional approved design assets, photographs, demonstration recordings and presentation materials can be added after review.

project.title: Ten Minutes
project.description: A real-time AI voice tarot consultation. Talk about a concern, choose cards, and explore what they mean with Lena.

sections.title: Product direction
paragraphs: Ten Minutes explores a low-friction way to discuss everyday concerns by voice. The first product emphasizes relationship questions while allowing open-ended consultation.
The experience is entertainment and reflection, not professional advice or a prediction of certain outcomes.

sections.title: Meet Lena
paragraphs: Lena is a confident, candid and playful tarot reader. She listens without forcing agreement, uses natural Korean speech, and encourages the user to make their own decisions.
The Queen mindset evolved from a bold character concept into a more nuanced balance of directness, warmth and independence.

sections.title: User journey
paragraphs: The mobile experience combines voice conversation with direct visual card selection. The user explains a concern, selects three cards and hears each interpretation before continuing the conversation.

tables.label: Consultation flow
rows: 01 Start
Enter the service and start a voice session.
02 Clarify
Discuss the concern and establish the question.
03 Choose
Select three cards directly on screen.
04 Read
Reveal and interpret each card in sequence.
05 Continue
Discuss follow-up questions and possible next steps.
06 Report
Close the time-bounded session and review the personal result.

rows: Time progression

items: The team explored Y2K, metallic and combined visual concepts and selected a metallic direction.
The design includes a character identity, a mobile call interface, individual card reveal and a personal report.
The deck contains 78 illustrations: 22 major and 56 minor arcana. The web assets are optimized and mapped to stable card identifiers.

rows: Voice consultation
Working prototype; naturalness and complete device acceptance require further review.
Card selection and reading
Three-card touchscreen selection and sequential reading are the initial flow.
Authentication

Report and sharing

Payments and expansion
Payment, additional readers and repeated draws are deferred.

research.title: Voice UX research
research.description: What we learned while designing a voice-first experience: when to speak, when to listen, and when a screen is better.

sections.title: Research questions
items: How can a voice agent respond naturally in Korean while maintaining a consistent character?
Which interactions are better performed by voice, and which need a visual interface?
How can the application keep model responses, card reveal and spoken playback aligned?

sections.title: Voice architecture trade-offs
paragraphs: The team investigated OpenAI, ElevenLabs and Typecast. The current design combines Realtime speech understanding and conversational reasoning with Typecast speech synthesis.
Direct model audio is a simpler route. A separate synthesis provider gives more control over the voice, but adds latency, cancellation and synchronization work.

tables.label: Voice UX decisions
rows: Spoken card numbers were difficult to recognize reliably.
Use direct touch for precise card selection.
Long explanations felt less conversational.
Prefer short utterances and wait for the user’s turn.
Card revelation and speech could fall out of sync.
Coordinate reading with application state and reveal events.
A hybrid voice pipeline can add response delay.
Evaluate timing, naturalness and interruption behavior together.

sections.title: Persona and prompt engineering
items: Separate the persona’s identity and values from operational instructions and reference knowledge.
Write example utterances for each consultation stage and spread.
Use manual editing and review to reduce repetitive, formal or overly elaborate AI phrasing.
Use versioned prompts and application-controlled tools to make changes reviewable.
Use a human-reviewed reference of 78 cards and connect the revealed card, question and position.

tables.label: Illustrative dialogue revisions

sections.title: Exploratory service research
paragraphs: Members experienced telephone, in-person and digital tarot services in November. We report only aggregate interaction observations, not personal concerns or individual provider assessments.

tables.label: Research observations
rows: Availability and entry
Reduce the friction of arranging a consultation.
Onboarding and context
Ask for the relevant context, not unnecessary personal information.
Card participation
Let users take part in the card selection and see the result.
Time constraints
Give an intentional closing rather than an unexpected end.
Voice comfort
Offer a low-pressure conversational opening and clear controls.
Persistent results
Give users an optional report to revisit the experience.

sections.title: Evaluation plan
paragraphs: The team observed qualitative behavior in exploratory tests. The following measures are proposed for future controlled evaluation; no quantitative benchmark or representative market result is claimed.

tables.label: Proposed evaluation measures
rows: Turn latency
Time from the end of user speech to the start of audible response.
Interruption success
Whether the old response stops and the new user turn is handled.
Task completion
Whether users complete question clarification, card selection, reading and report.
Persona consistency
Whether speech retains Lena’s character across scenarios.
Naturalness
Qualitative rating of pacing, wording and conversational turn-taking.
